import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyExteriorZero
import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyExteriorRange
import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyPoint
import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyTorusExteriorRanks

/-!
# The exterior cup comparison for finite tori

The empty finite product of circles is a point. Splitting off one circle
and using the actual circle-product cup formula then proves that all
cohomology classes on a finite torus are sums of iterated degree-one cups.
Equal finite free ranks then make the exterior cup comparison bijective.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

namespace Mumford.Analytic

private instance finZeroCircleSubsingleton : Subsingleton (Fin 0 → Circle) :=
  ⟨fun _ _ => funext fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩

private instance finZeroCirclePathConnected : PathConnectedSpace (Fin 0 → Circle) :=
  ⟨⟨fun _ => 1⟩, fun _ _ => ⟨Path.pi fun i => Fin.elim0 i⟩⟩

/-- The exterior cup comparison is surjective on the empty product of circles. -/
theorem finiteTorusExteriorPower_zero_dimensional_surjective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Surjective
      (singularCohomologyExteriorPower (TopCat.of (Fin 0 → Circle)) n) := by
  cases n with
  | zero =>
      exact (singularCohomologyExteriorPower_zero_bijective
        (TopCat.of (Fin 0 → Circle))).2
  | succ n =>
      intro b
      refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
      rw [map_zero, integralSingularCohomology_eq_zero_of_subsingleton b]

/-- Integral cohomology of a finite torus is generated by degree-one cups. -/
theorem torusCohomologyExteriorPower_surjective (d n : ℕ) :
    Function.Surjective
      (singularCohomologyExteriorPower (TopCat.of (Fin d → Circle)) n) := by
  induction d generalizing n with
  | zero => exact finiteTorusExteriorPower_zero_dimensional_surjective n
  | succ d ih =>
      cases n with
      | zero =>
          letI : PathConnectedSpace (Fin (d + 1) → Circle) :=
            ⟨⟨fun _ => 1⟩, fun x y =>
              ⟨Path.pi (fun i => PathConnectedSpace.somePath (x i) (y i))⟩⟩
          exact (singularCohomologyExteriorPower_zero_bijective
            (TopCat.of (Fin (d + 1) → Circle))).2
      | succ n =>
          apply singularCohomologyExteriorPower_surjective_of_pullback
            (TopCat.ofHom (finSuccCircleHomeomorph d).toHomotopyEquiv.toFun) (n + 1)
            (singularCohomologyHomotopyEquiv
              (X := TopCat.of (Fin (d + 1) → Circle))
              (Y := TopCat.of ((Fin d → Circle) × Circle))
              (finSuccCircleHomeomorph d).toHomotopyEquiv (n + 1)).surjective
          exact circleProductCohomologyExteriorPower_surjective
            (TopCat.of (Fin d → Circle)) 1 n (ih n) (ih (n + 1))

/-- Cup product identifies the exterior powers of integral first cohomology
with integral cohomology in every degree of a finite torus. -/
theorem torusCohomologyExteriorPower_bijective (d n : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective
      (singularCohomologyExteriorPower (TopCat.of (Fin d → Circle)) n) :=
  torusCohomologyExteriorPower_bijective_of_surjective d n
    (torusCohomologyExteriorPower_surjective d n)

/-- The exterior cup equivalence for a finite product of circles. -/
def torusCohomologyExteriorPowerEquiv (d n : ℕ) :
    (⋀[ℤ]^n (IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of (Fin d → Circle)) 1)) ≃ₗ[ℤ]
      IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of (Fin d → Circle)) n :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective _ (torusCohomologyExteriorPower_bijective d n)

@[simp]
theorem torusCohomologyExteriorPowerEquiv_apply (d n : ℕ)
    (x : ⋀[ℤ]^n (IntegralSingularCohomology (TopCat.of (Fin d → Circle)) 1)) :
    torusCohomologyExteriorPowerEquiv d n x =
      singularCohomologyExteriorPower (TopCat.of (Fin d → Circle)) n x := rfl

end Mumford.Analytic
